chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from al-Sayyari, from Ubaydullah ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) wrote from Khurasan to Medina: 'Do not give Abu Ja'far the second Suweeq with sugar, for it is a destruction for the men.'

key_terms.السَّوِيق: Suweeq, a traditional food made from roasted flour, often mixed with water or milk.
key_terms.خُرَاسَانَ: Khurasan, a historical region in Persia/Iran.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on giving sugar to Suweeq according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical medical wisdom of Imam al-Rida (AS), who identified that sugar, while sweet, was considered 'heavy' or detrimental to the digestive health of men in that era. It reflects the broader Shia tradition of integrating spiritual guidance with empirical health advice, where the Imams provided specific dietary prescriptions tailored to individual constitutions and contemporary understanding of physiology.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Al Sayyari, from Ubeydullah Bin Abu Abdullah having said:
‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> wrote from Khurasan to Al-Medina: ‘Do not let Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup> to drink Al-Suweyq with the sugar, for it is a destruction for the men’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Musa ibn al-Hassan from al-Sayyariy from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:

“Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, wrote from Khurasan to al-Madinah, ‘Do not make abu Ja‘far al- Thaniy to drink sawiq with sugar because it is bad for man.’ “Al-Sayyariy has explained it from ‘Ubayd Allah that it is undesirable for men because it weakens manhood desire due to its cold nature with sugar.”
